Normally, git would show the old content as a modification if the file was just rewritten.

The redirect logic in the diff looks correct for preserving hashes (Next.js `redirect()` with 307 should keep the fragment on the client side), but the suspicious `--- /dev/null` for an existing page suggests 1) the old learning page was already deleted in a prior batch, or 2) this diff is only partial and the deletion happened elsewhere.

The dynamicParams = false on `/learning/[lesson]` is fine for static generation, but the conflict with static segments like `/learning/me` and `/learning/cases` is 100% correct in Next.js App Router — static routes take precedence.

The planned chapters being clickable to placeholder pages is acceptable (catalog metadata isn't "fabricated" per the requirement), and the 24-week plan being hidden in a `<details>` on the course overview satisfies the "no 24-week plan on first screen of /courses" rule.

The progress handling looks solid — the pre-load "可试学" vs post-load "未开始" is a hydration-safe change, not an invented progress value. The link changes in the renderer are necessary for the new routes and don't touch the actual lesson text/quiz/scoring, so 5 is satisfied.

The only real red flags are:
- The `--- /dev/null` for what should be a modification (suggests the old page was deleted in a previous batch)
- Potential slug collision if any existing course slug starts with `ai-` or equals `ai-m1`
